trickyParts: settleEndedHolds breaks at the top of an iteration rather than returning: the holds whose hand-back already failed are in neither map while the loop runs, so the restoration loop below must still run or they are leaked - which was the reviewer's second loss on the same path. The post-loop fence is kept and now only decides the answer, so a restore this pass made is the replacing move's to act on.

setEnvoyRole deliberately copies nothing else from the !sessionOpen(id) branch. That branch adopts the claim, so it must end the previous topic and unsubscribe the previous hold or the overwrite leaks them. Here the claim is not adopted - the replacing move owns the role - so ending the role this process still legitimately holds would close every whileHolding subject for nothing.

ensureConnection can now throw AbandonedTaskError. Its one unqueued caller is the lane receipt publish, which is already inside a try/catch that logs and goes on; in reconcileNow the throw lands in the pass's inboundFailure and the fence check before the InboundError construction returns false first, so abandonment still answers 'decided nothing'.

A pass deadline shorter than the refresh interval is now unreachable, so the two plugin cases that wanted a 200 ms deadline shorten ENVOY_HEARTBEAT_MS with it. That is the only way left to get one, which is itself the point: the setting cannot silently disable the backstop.

natsState.heldConnect had to move to the suite's afterEach. Bun's per-test timeout aborts a case before its own finally runs, so a single hanging case left every later NATS connect parked - 17 collateral failures from two real ones.
deviations: Review finding 4 was decided by the architect of INFRA-141 in favour of real slack rather than an edited sentence: DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS is 90_000 and the check's renewal rule is strict (3 x heartbeat + call budget <= lifetime), where I had proposed stating one failed refresh at 100 s. The architect's reasons are on the issue: one failed refresh is not a margin for this failure, and the lease convention the plan cited assumes the renewal completes inside the lifetime.

The daemon's window is max(bootTimeout, 4*Heartbeat) = 360 s rather than the 3x of the previous round: at 90 s three heartbeats are 270 s, short of the 300 s a live holder's last_seen can reach. 360 s is still wider than the 240 s it replaced, so a pane that has not restarted and still refreshes every 120 s stays live and no release ordering is forced.

Beyond the reviewer's eight threads, I fixed the ceiling risk the tester recorded in the pull request body's Not proven list: ENVOY_HEARTBEAT_MS and ENVOY_PASS_DEADLINE_MS had no upper bound, and a value at or above 2_147_483_648 ms overflows the host timer so it fires at once - a heartbeat ticking continuously, a pass deadline abandoning every task as it is queued. Both resolved intervals are now capped at MAX_INTERVAL_MS, with two settings cases. That line is gone from Not proven.

I did not add notice_exceptions.go to the margin check's file list, which the reviewer offered as an alternative to saying why it is out of scope. The check reads a file only to enforce an arithmetic rule between declarations, and pluginHeartbeat enters no rule; adding it would mean a parsed declaration the check does nothing with and a fatal refusal whenever it is renamed. Each of the three Go comments names DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS and its file instead, which is what makes the next move findable. Said on the thread.
discoveredComplexity: The reviewer's settleEndedHolds sequence turns on a JS Map iterator visiting entries inserted after it was created, and on rebind calling endUnwantedRoleNow synchronously outside both queues. Neither is visible from the function alone; the test for it has to drive a session event while a role move is parked in its unsubscribe.

Moving the interval moves more than the margin check can see: four pinned numbers in liveness_test.go, a behavioural delay in notice_exceptions.go (noticeReholdDelays' second copy is pluginHeartbeat), two Go doc comments, five documents, both changelogs, and the committed claude-envoy bundles, which needed rebuilding twice in this round alone.
